emma (eng-runtime): heads-up — after yesterday's kernel routing tweak we saw a spike in OOMs on p40-40g pools and much worse tail latencies. seems tied to KV cache pressure + fragmentation :eyes:

ravi (eng-runtime): can you paste the flame/profile? was this only after the kernel selector change or also batching tweaks?

emma (eng-runtime): attaching short excerpt from the profiler and a heap map. main signals: lower kv-hit-rate (~8% drop), more small free slots, workspace allocations larger on average. nvtop shows steady mem high-water.

nora (eng-ml): interesting — could be that the new kernel prefers larger workspace buffers, fragmenting the slab for KV prefill. we saw similar in the 0.8->0.9 cycle but we fixed with coalescing.

sam (eng-sre): logs:```
[2026-03-05T14:22:11Z] request 0x7f12: prefill allocate 48MB slab id=23
[2026-03-05T14:22:11Z] request 0x7f12: decode allocate 8MB slab id=42
[2026-03-05T14:22:11Z] OOM allocating 12MB workspace
```

emma (eng-runtime): exact. per-request prefill cap was bumped up to 48MB by the selector (to reduce retries), but it leaves lots of 8–16MB holes that the KV slab allocator can't pack.

ravi (eng-runtime): hypothesis: kernel selection has widened workspace size distribution; batching heuristics now create richer long-context jobs that prefill bigger KVs. eviction strategy still favors LRU for prefill keys which keeps them resident and blocks coalescing.

nora (eng-ml): two quick mitigations to try: 1) reduce per-request prefill cap to 16MB (fallback to on-demand for >cap), 2) enable small-slot coalescing/compaction on allocate free path. both cheap to A/B.

sam (eng-sre): agree. also suggest a temporary change to eviction policy to prefer demoting prefill keys older than 1m or those with low decode-hit rates (prefill-heavy), so we avoid keeping big prefill blobs.

alloc-bot: perf-test queued: slab-coalesce-disabled -> baseline, slab-coalesce-enabled -> experiment. 1000 req mix (50% long, 50% short). ETA ~ 2h.

emma (eng-runtime): quick config snippet I tested locally:```
cache:
  per_request_prefill_cap_mb: 16
  eviction:
    prefer_demote:
      - tag: "prefill"
        min_age_s: 60
  allocator:
    enable_coalesce_free: true
    small_slot_size_kb: 8
    merge_threshold: 3
```

ravi (eng-runtime): nice. if coalescing works we should see drop in fragmentation metric (free-run-holes) and recover KV hit by ~5–10%. also check CPU impact of compaction on hot path.

nora (eng-ml): for kernel selection side, we can add a soft cap that prefers kernels with smaller workspace when the host free-frag > 30% to avoid making fragmentation worse. ie routing policy interacts with allocator metrics.

sam (eng-sre): can we gate that by a watermark? host_free_frag is noisy; maybe use a 1-min EWMA. I'll add alert if free_frag > 40% for >2min.

emma (eng-runtime): alloc-bot results in: experiment -> 40% reduction in OOMs, KV hit restored ~6%, tail p95 decode latency down 18%. small CPU bump ~2%. config above rolled to canary.

ravi (eng-runtime): great. next steps: a) keep coalesce in canary for 48h b) implement kernel-selection soft cap (nora) c) create perf test that simulates mixed prefill/decode mix to avoid regression.

nora (eng-ml): I'll prototype the kernel-routing hook today with EWMA threshold. if we see regressions, we can fallback to previous behavior via routing weight.

sam (eng-sre): ops: add a temporary per-request metric (prefill_alloc_mb) to the console and add a dashboard tile for free_frag and kv_hit by host pool.

emma (eng-runtime): thanks — i'll make the PR for the allocator coalesce and the per-request cap. keeping the canary pinned to p40-40g for now. :thumbsup:

ravi (eng-runtime): one caution: coalescing can increase latency variance on tight requests if compaction runs synchronously. prefer background async compaction or cooperative compaction during idle decode cycles.

emma (eng-runtime): noted. initial coalesce is opportunistic on free path then schedule async compaction. will document in PR.

sam (eng-sre): will monitor. thanks team.

alloc-bot: canary monitoring: OOM rate, kv_hit_rate, p95_decode_latency, host_free_frag. will post results in 2h.
